main_text.p: Sustentans est membrum reliquas corporis partes suo robore sustinens vel muniens.
Sustentatio hæc est cum fulcimenti & stabilimenti, tum munimenti & firmamenti.
Proinde anima hoc membro utitur ad corpus, ejus reliqua membra tam munienda & firmanda, ut tuta & firma sint, quam stabilienda & fulcienda, ut sic sustentata consistant.
Membrum sustentans est primi generis, vel secundi.
Primi generis sustinens membrum est Os[?].
Os,Os est membrum sustinens durissimum & siccissimum. In ossibus spectantur Partes, & Conjunctio.
Ossium partes,Pars Ossis adnata ossi ἀπόφυσις[?] ac appendix dicitur.
Pars prominentior tuberculi instar ex osse procedens ἐπίφυσις[?] & processus dicitur.
Pars alterius ossis cavum subiens, Caput dicitur

page.notes: The line "Os:" overlapping the end of the preceding line is partly obscured; read as a line-initial "Os" with [?]. The Greek terms ἀπόφυσις and ἐπίφυσις are read from a small, somewhat blurred print and are uncertain. Show-through from the reverse side is present throughout and was excluded. The page-top line "Estq;" is a fragment continuing the previous paragraph.
